name: Copperveil Switchback Crowd-Runner Set
description: A reversible mid-length jacket anchors this set — one side a muted copper-brown twill with faint diagonal texture, the other a washed slate-grey microweave that reads as generic transit worker at a glance. The jacket features a split-back panel with magnetic detach seams at the shoulder blades, accommodating tail geneware or spinal rig hardware without bunching. Concealed inside-chest channels run parallel to the sternum for flat holster inserts or folded tools, and a hidden inner hem pocket spans the full width of the back panel. Beneath it, a dense rust-amber henley in scanner-resistant polymerized cotton sits close to the body, collar high enough to obscure a neck-line neural port. The trousers are straight-leg in dark ochre canvas with reinforced kneepad pockets (empty by default, functional when loaded) and two thigh channels for quick-draw tool access. Footwear is a low-profile boot in oil-tanned synthetic leather, cork-composite sole for reduced acoustic signature on hard floors, ankle-height with a side-zip hidden under a fold of material. The whole look reads as a mid-Circuit shift worker running an errand — until the jacket flips.
functionality: Reversible jacket for rapid identity shift; split-back panel with magnetic detach seams for spinal rigs and tail geneware; dual sternum holster channels; full-width hidden hem pocket; thigh-channel trousers for tool access; reinforced knee pockets; low acoustic-signature footwear; scanner-resistant base layer
what_it_says: This person moves through crowds without snagging attention. The copper tones say working-class practicality, not poverty. The jacket flip says they've done this before. Runners who wear this are methodical, patient, and prefer to be three blocks gone before anyone knows a job happened.
worn_by: mid-tier fixers working below their usual grade
manufacturer: Driftmark Collective — unlicensed street label, Circuit District, M88
story_hooks: A runner flips the jacket mid-pursuit and walks past the pursuing security team — but the copper side has a distinctive repair patch their contact will recognize, blowing the switch.

The scanner-resistant henley is flagging at a checkpoint because someone swapped the genuine article with a knockoff — now the runner needs to bluff through a hand-scan with a concealed weapon in the sternum channel.
A fixer spots the Driftmark Collective label inside the jacket collar and immediately knows the runner's tier — raising or lowering their offered rate accordingly.
